1.web: Guard your steps when you go to God’s house; for to draw near to listen is better than to give the sacrifice of fools, for they don’t know that they do evil.
1.asv: Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God; for to draw nigh to hear is better than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they know not that they do evil.

2.web: Don’t be rash with your mouth, and don’t let your heart be hasty to utter anything before God; for God is in heaven, and you on earth. Therefore let your words be few.
2.asv: Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thy heart be hasty to utter anything before God; for God is in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few.

3.web: For as a dream comes with a multitude of cares, so a fool’s speech with a multitude of words.
3.asv: For a dream cometh with a multitude of business, and a fool’s voice with a multitude of words.

4.web: When you vow a vow to God, don’t defer to pay it; for he has no pleasure in fools. Pay that which you vow.
4.asv: When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou vowest.

5.web: It is better that you should not vow, than that you should vow and not pay.
5.asv: Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.

6.web: Don’t allow your mouth to lead you into sin. Don’t protest before the messenger that this was a mistake. Why should God be angry at your voice, and destroy the work of your hands?
6.asv: Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error: wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thy hands?

7.web: For in the multitude of dreams there are vanities, as well as in many words: but you must fear God.
7.asv: For in the multitude of dreams there are vanities, and in many words: but fear thou God.

8.web: If you see the oppression of the poor, and the violent taking away of justice and righteousness in a district, don’t marvel at the matter: for one official is eyed by a higher one; and there are officials over them.
8.asv: If thou seest the oppression of the poor, and the violent taking away of justice and righteousness in a province, marvel not at the matter: for one higher than the high regardeth; and there are higher than they.

9.web: Moreover the profit of the earth is for all. The king profits from the field.
9.asv: Moreover the profit of the earth is for all: the king himself is served by the field.

10.web: He who loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he who loves abundance, with increase: this also is vanity.
10.asv: He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loveth abundance, with increase: this also is vanity.

11.web: When goods increase, those who eat them are increased; and what advantage is there to its owner, except to feast on them with his eyes?
11.asv: When goods increase, they are increased that eat them; and what advantage is there to the owner thereof, save the beholding of them with his eyes?

12.web: The sleep of a laboring man is sweet, whether he eats little or much; but the abundance of the rich will not allow him to sleep.
12.asv: The sleep of a laboring man is sweet, whether he eat little or much; but the fulness of the rich will not suffer him to sleep.

13.web: There is a grievous evil which I have seen under the sun: wealth kept by its owner to his harm.
13.asv: There is a grievous evil which I have seen under the sun, namely, riches kept by the owner thereof to his hurt:

14.web: Those riches perish by misfortune, and if he has fathered a son, there is nothing in his hand.
14.asv: and those riches perish by evil adventure; and if he hath begotten a son, there is nothing in his hand.

15.web: As he came out of his mother’s womb, naked shall he go again as he came, and shall take nothing for his labor, which he may carry away in his hand.
15.asv: As he came forth from his mother’s womb, naked shall he go again as he came, and shall take nothing for his labor, which he may carry away in his hand.

16.web: This also is a grievous evil, that in all points as he came, so shall he go. And what profit does he have who labors for the wind?
16.asv: And this also is a grievous evil, that in all points as he came, so shall he go: and what profit hath he that he laboreth for the wind?

17.web: All his days he also eats in darkness, he is frustrated, and has sickness and wrath.
17.asv: All his days also he eateth in darkness, and he is sore vexed, and hath sickness and wrath.

18.web: Behold, that which I have seen to be good and proper is for one to eat and to drink, and to enjoy good in all his labor, in which he labors under the sun, all the days of his life which God has given him; for this is his portion.
18.asv: Behold, that which I have seen to be good and to be comely is for one to eat and to drink, and to enjoy good in all his labor, wherein he laboreth under the sun, all the days of his life which God hath given him: for this is his portion.

19.web: Every man also to whom God has given riches and wealth, and has given him power to eat of it, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labor—this is the gift of God.
19.asv: Every man also to whom God hath given riches and wealth, and hath given him power to eat thereof, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labor—this is the gift of God.

20.web: For he shall not often reflect on the days of his life; because God occupies him with the joy of his heart.
20.asv: For he shall not much remember the days of his life; because God answereth him in the joy of his heart.
